The story of a woman in Bengal—who worked in other people's homes—rising to become a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is truly remarkable! Kalita Majhi, who worked as a domestic helper, has been elected as the MLA from the Ausgram assembly constituency in West Bengal. Her victory coincides with the significant success achieved by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the state. Kalita Majhi defeated the TMC's Shyama Prasanna Lohar by a margin of 12,535 votes. Residing in a narrow lane in Ghuskura Machhpur Para in Bardhaman—located about three hours away from Kolkata—Kalita Majhi was working as a domestic helper until just a few days ago. For Kalita Majhi—who supported her family through manual labor—entering politics and achieving success is nothing short of astonishing, particularly in an era when engaging in politics has become a highly expensive endeavor. Kalita Majhi recounts, "I served as the party's booth agent in 2014. Subsequently, in 2019, I was entrusted with responsibilities within the Ghuskura town unit; I served as the town's party secretary. Then, in 2021, the party nominated me as a candidate for the assembly elections."

media:group.media:title: क्या ममता टाल देंगी BJP की शपथ ? #shorts #youtubeshorts by Dr. #arvindarora
media:group.media:description:
The path for the BJP to form a government in Bengal is not as easy as initially anticipated. Typically, following election results, a defeated Chief Minister tenders their resignation on moral grounds; however, breaking with this tradition, Mamata Banerjee has refused to step down from her post. Mamata argued that the electoral process was marred by massive rigging and that she intends to remain in office until an investigation into the matter is conducted. When Mamata Banerjee refused to resign, Governor R.N. Ravi took decisive action, invoking Article 174(2)(b) of the Constitution. On May 7, the Governor issued an order dissolving the Legislative Assembly. Now, the question arises: can the Supreme Court issue a stay order on the May 9 swearing-in ceremony in response to Mamata Banerjee's petition? Legal experts suggest that the Court generally refrains from interfering in a mandate backed by an "overwhelming majority." If the BJP commands the support of 207 MLAs, the Court is unlikely to halt the process of government formation. However, should substantial evidence of a grave constitutional lapse or electoral malpractice within the process come to light, the Court could issue a "status quo" order. Nevertheless, the likelihood of this occurring is negligible.
